objects.description: Mapping structure for non-overlapping half-open address ranges [addr, addr+size) to string labels, with optional cross-domain translation to a second address space. Provides insertion of ranges (including dual ranges with translation), queries (coverage, lookup, size), translation, compression of adjacent identical labels, iteration utilities, and a rollup over multiple maps that must share identical domain coverage. Move-only; copying is disabled. Unknown size is represented by kUnknownSize. Internal storage is a std::map<uint64_t, Entry>.
Forward declaration of a test fixture/class used for unit testing RangeMap. No definition is provided in this header.

functions.name: bloaty::RangeMap::RangeMap
functions.description: Default-constructs an empty RangeMap with no ranges and no translations. Typical usage: create a RangeMap instance before adding ranges via AddRange/AddDualRange.
requirements: Object is initially empty; no other preconditions.

functions.name: bloaty::RangeMap::operator=
functions.description: Move-assigns from other, replacing the contents of this RangeMap with those of other. After assignment, other is left in a valid but unspecified state.
requirements: other must be an rvalue (moved-from) RangeMap.

functions.name: bloaty::RangeMap::AddRange
functions.signature: void bloaty::RangeMap::AddRange(uint64_t addr, uint64_t size, const std::string& val)
functions.description: Adds a labeled range [addr, addr + size) to this map in the primary domain. Ranges in a RangeMap must be non-overlapping. Intended to build up the address-to-label mapping before queries or translations.
requirements: Ranges added to this map must be non-overlapping with existing ranges.
addr + size must not overflow 64-bit unsigned arithmetic; the implementation asserts internal consistency.
size should represent the exact length of the range in bytes; behavior for size == 0 is unspecified.

functions.name: bloaty::RangeMap::AddDualRange
functions.signature: void bloaty::RangeMap::AddDualRange(uint64_t addr, uint64_t size, uint64_t otheraddr, const std::string& val)
functions.description: Adds a labeled range [addr, addr + size) to this map (domain D1) and records that it corresponds to a range starting at otheraddr in a different domain (D2). This establishes translation metadata used by Translate and AddRangeWithTranslation.
requirements: Ranges added to this map must be non-overlapping with existing ranges.
addr + size must not overflow 64-bit unsigned arithmetic; the implementation asserts internal consistency.
otheraddr is the start of the corresponding range in the other domain; its validity is not otherwise checked here.

functions.name: bloaty::RangeMap::AddRangeWithTranslation
functions.signature: bool bloaty::RangeMap::AddRangeWithTranslation(uint64_t addr, uint64_t size, const std::string& val, const bloaty::RangeMap& translator, bool verbose, bloaty::RangeMap* other)
functions.description: Adds a range [addr, addr + size) with label val to this map (domain D1) and simultaneously adds corresponding translated ranges to other (domain D2) using translator (domain D1) to translate D1→D2 based on prior AddDualRange calls on translator. Returns true if the entire [addr, addr + size) was present in translator. If false, the contents of this and other are documented as undefined and the caller should abort using these maps.
requirements: translator must contain translation metadata (from prior AddDualRange calls) that covers the entire [addr, addr + size) in its domain for a successful return.
Callers must check the boolean return value; if false, both this and other must not be used further as their contents are undefined.
other must be a non-null pointer to a RangeMap to receive translated ranges.
Ranges added to this map must be non-overlapping with existing ranges.
addr + size must not overflow 64-bit unsigned arithmetic.
verbose controls diagnostic logging only; no functional preconditions.

functions.name: bloaty::RangeMap::Compress
functions.description: Collapses adjacent ranges that have the same label to reduce memory usage and noise when dumping full maps. No effect on aggregate reporting where identical labels are summed.
requirements: The map should be in a consistent, non-overlapping state prior to calling.
May be called any time after range insertion to coalesce adjacent same-labeled regions.

functions.name: bloaty::RangeMap::CoversRange
functions.signature: bool bloaty::RangeMap::CoversRange(uint64_t addr, uint64_t size) const
functions.description: Returns true if this RangeMap fully covers the range [addr, addr + size) with one or more of its ranges; false otherwise.
requirements: addr and size define the half-open interval [addr, addr + size).
addr + size must be representable in 64-bit unsigned arithmetic (no overflow).

functions.name: bloaty::RangeMap::GetMaxAddress
functions.description: Returns the maximum address contained in this map (the greatest end address of any stored range).
requirements: Meaningful only when the map is non-empty; behavior for an empty map is not documented in this header.

functions.name: bloaty::RangeMap::Translate
functions.signature: bool bloaty::RangeMap::Translate(uint64_t addr, uint64_t* translated) const
functions.description: Translates addr from this map's domain into the corresponding address in the other domain using previously established dual-range metadata. Returns true on success and writes the translated address via translated.
requirements: translated must be a non-null pointer to receive the result.
A translation must have been established (via AddDualRange on the relevant entries); otherwise returns false.

functions.name: bloaty::RangeMap::TryGetLabel
functions.signature: bool bloaty::RangeMap::TryGetLabel(uint64_t addr, std::string* label) const
functions.description: If a stored range contains addr, sets label to that range’s label and returns true; otherwise returns false and leaves label unspecified.
requirements: label must be a non-null pointer.
addr is interpreted in the primary domain of this map.

functions.name: bloaty::RangeMap::TryGetLabelForRange
functions.signature: bool bloaty::RangeMap::TryGetLabelForRange(uint64_t addr, uint64_t size, std::string* label) const
functions.description: If a stored range fully covers [addr, addr + size), sets label to that range’s label and returns true; otherwise returns false.
requirements: label must be a non-null pointer.
addr + size must be representable in 64-bit unsigned arithmetic (no overflow).

functions.name: bloaty::RangeMap::TryGetSize
functions.signature: bool bloaty::RangeMap::TryGetSize(uint64_t addr, uint64_t* size) const
functions.description: If a stored range starts exactly at addr, writes that range’s size to size and returns true; otherwise returns false.
requirements: size must be a non-null pointer.
addr must equal the exact start of a stored range for success.

functions.name: bloaty::RangeMap::DebugString
functions.description: Returns a human-readable debug string describing the contents of the RangeMap. Useful for diagnostics and unit testing.

functions.name: bloaty::RangeMap::EntryDebugString
functions.signature: static std::string bloaty::RangeMap::EntryDebugString(uint64_t addr, uint64_t size, uint64_t other_start, const std::string& label)
functions.description: Formats a single entry as a debug string: [addr, end) (size=...) : label, optionally including other_start if a translation exists. Used for diagnostics.
requirements: addr and size should correspond to a valid stored entry semantics in the map using half-open intervals.
When size equals bloaty::RangeMap::kUnknownSize, end is rendered as '?'.

functions.name: bloaty::RangeMap::EntryDebugString
functions.signature: template <class T> std::string bloaty::RangeMap::EntryDebugString(T it) const
functions.description: Formats the entry pointed to by iterator it as a debug string. If it equals mappings_.end(), returns "[end]". Otherwise delegates to the static EntryDebugString overload.
requirements: it must be a valid iterator comparable to this->mappings_.end() and, if not end(), must reference an entry from this RangeMap.

functions.name: bloaty::RangeMap::ComputeRollup
functions.signature: template <class Func> static void bloaty::RangeMap::ComputeRollup(const std::vector<const bloaty::RangeMap*>& range_maps, Func func)
functions.description: Iterates over multiple RangeMaps in lockstep, partitioning their common covered domain into contiguous subranges where labels are stable, and invokes func(keys, start, end) for each subrange. keys is a vector<string> of the current labels, one per map. All input maps must cover exactly the same domain.
requirements: range_maps.size() must be > 0.
If range_maps[0] (the base map) is empty, all other maps must also be empty; otherwise a runtime_error is thrown.
All non-empty input maps must cover exactly the same domain without gaps; mismatches cause assertions and runtime_error exceptions.
func must be callable with (const std::vector<std::string>& keys, uint64_t start, uint64_t end).

functions.name: bloaty::RangeMap::ForEachRange
functions.signature: template <class Func> void bloaty::RangeMap::ForEachRange(Func func) const
functions.description: Invokes func(start, size) for each stored range in ascending address order.
requirements: func must be callable with (uint64_t start, uint64_t size).
Iteration order is ascending by start address; func should not modify the RangeMap.

functions.name: bloaty::RangeMap::ForEachRangeWithStart
functions.signature: template <class Func> void bloaty::RangeMap::ForEachRangeWithStart(uint64_t start, Func func) const
functions.description: Starting from the range that contains start (or the next one), iterates forward and calls func(label, addr, size) for each range until func returns false or the end is reached. Allows early termination based on the callback return value.
requirements: func must be callable with (const std::string& label, uint64_t addr, uint64_t size) and return a boolean-like value; returning false stops iteration.
start is used to find the containing or next range; if no such range exists, no callbacks are invoked.
func must not modify the RangeMap.
